routines.semantics: Pushes the supplied module onto the CSPICE traceback stack; nested names appear in captured error trace. Empty names signal EMPTYSTRING. Blank/mismatched/overflow trace misuse emits diagnostic text rather than normal signaled exceptions.

Named error cases require the matching diagnostic, not merely two failures.

routines.errorAssessment: Empty-string or invalid-selector cases require stable error fragments. Selector restriction is a typed wrapper policy on both oracle and tspice. Trace mismatch/underflow/overflow diagnostics write to the disabled output device, rather than producing ordinary SPICE failures, so they are not misrepresented as thrown-error cases.
routines.fixtureRationale: No kernels or datasets required; all strings, nested module labels, and overlength ASCII messages are project-authored synthetic inputs.
routines.cleanup: Raw errors are captured/reset in the shared shim before throwing. Oracle capture obtains actual CSPICE messages/trace then resets in finally to model that documented policy. Case lifecycle calls kclear/reset before/after, clients dispose in finally, and each oracle workflow runs in its own process. Tests compare the next signal to detect stale state; WASM strings/output/error allocations are freed on every allocation failure. Trace entries are tracked per case and unwound in reverse order by a finalizer on success/failure; reset alone does not pop them. Direct same-instance tests check the next case has no leaked trace.
routines.tolerance: No numeric tolerance dependence: booleans, full strings, exact object keys/shapes and null effects compare exactly. Trace formatting is the shared CSPICE qcktrc output. No global or local tolerance changes.

findings.summary: The first full native lane failed nine new cases because active user trace names survived reset and leaked into later cases. WASM fresh instances and separate oracle processes hid that lifecycle gap.
